deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument controls Terraform resource lifecycle behaviour. PREVENT, DELETE and ABANDON determine whether Terraform can destroy the resource or remove it from state, but they do not directly affect authentication, authorization, encryption, confidentiality, integrity, or exposure of the GRPC route. Therefore, this argument is operational rather than security impacting.

description.description: A free-text description of the resource. Max length 1024 characters.
description.rationale: Free-text descriptions do not affect the routing behavior or security properties of the GrpcRoute. Enforcing descriptions addresses audit and operational concerns, not the security of this resource's configuration.

gateways.description: List of gateways this GrpcRoute is attached to, as one of the routing rules to route the requests served by the gateway.
gateways.rationale: Gateways are references to other resources. Constraining them requires knowing specific gateway names/IDs, which violates the multi-tenant model. Gateway selection is team-owned configuration, not a platform security control.

hostnames.description: Required. Service hostnames with an optional port for which this route describes traffic.
hostnames.rationale: Hostnames are service identifiers tied to specific workloads. Mandating which hostnames a team's route can serve is overreach—that choice belongs to the team operating the service.

labels.description:
Set of label tags associated with the GrpcRoute resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are metadata for resource organization and cost allocation. They do not affect the routing behavior or security properties of the GrpcRoute itself. Label enforcement addresses governance and compliance, not the security of this resource's configuration.

location.description: Location (region) of the GRPCRoute resource to be created. Only the value 'global' is currently allowed; defaults to 'global' if omitted.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

meshes.description: List of meshes this GrpcRoute is attached to, as one of the routing rules to route the requests served by the mesh.
meshes.rationale: Meshes are specific resource references/pointers. Constraining them requires knowing specific mesh names/IDs, which violates the core multi-tenant principle of generic policies.

name.rationale: The resource name is an identifier for tracking and reference. It does not affect the routing behavior, traffic handling, or security properties of the GrpcRoute itself. Naming conventions are operational and governance concerns, not security of this resource's configuration.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project is a resource identifier/reference, which the mental model explicitly places out of scope. Whitelisting specific projects assumes team-specific boundaries—overreach.

rules.description: Rules that define how traffic is routed and handled.

rules.action.description: Required. A detailed rule defining how to route traffic.

rules.action.timeout.description: Specifies the timeout for selected route.
rules.action.timeout.rationale: Timeout controls request handling duration and affects operational resilience and performance. It does not directly constrain what backends can be routed to or how traffic is secured. Timeout enforcement is a capacity/availability concern, not a security property of this resource.

rules.action.destinations.description: The destination to which traffic should be forwarded.

rules.action.destinations.service_name.description: The URL of a BackendService to route traffic to.
rules.action.destinations.service_name.rationale: service_name is a reference to a backend service resource. References are out of scope; constraining it requires knowing team-specific resource IDs.

rules.action.destinations.weight.description: Specifies the proportion of requests forwarded to the backend referenced by the serviceName field.
rules.action.destinations.weight.rationale: Weight specifies traffic distribution across backends for load balancing. This is an operational concern affecting performance and availability, not the security boundary of which backends can receive traffic.

rules.action.fault_injection_policy.description: The specification for fault injection introduced into traffic to test the resiliency of clients to backend service failure.

rules.action.fault_injection_policy.abor.description: Specification of how client requests are aborted as part of fault injection before being sent to a destination.
The HTTP status code used to abort the request.
rules.action.fault_injection_policy.abor.rationale: HTTP status codes for fault injection are testing configuration used to simulate failures. This affects testing resilience, not the security of the resource itself.

rules.action.fault_injection_policy.abor.description: The percentage of traffic which will be aborted.
rules.action.fault_injection_policy.abor.rationale: Percentage of traffic to abort is a testing parameter for chaos engineering. It does not affect the security boundary or routing behavior in production.

rules.action.fault_injection_policy.dela.description: Specification of how client requests are delayed as part of fault injection before being sent to a destination.
Specify a fixed delay before forwarding the request.
rules.action.fault_injection_policy.dela.rationale: Fixed delay is a testing/operational parameter used to simulate latency. It does not affect the security properties of this routing configuration.

rules.action.fault_injection_policy.dela.description: The percentage of traffic on which delay will be injected.
rules.action.fault_injection_policy.dela.rationale: Percentage of traffic to delay is a testing operational configuration, not a security constraint on this resource.

rules.action.retry_policy.description: Specifies the retry policy associated with this route.

rules.action.retry_policy.num_retries.description: Specifies the allowed number of retries.
rules.action.retry_policy.num_retries.rationale: Retry count is an availability and resilience control affecting how the system responds to transient failures. It is operational, not a security property of the routing configuration.

rules.action.retry_policy.retry_conditio.description: Specifies one or more conditions when this retry policy applies. Possible values: ["connect-failure", "refused-stream", "cancelled", "deadline-exceeded", "resource-exhausted", "unavailable"]
rules.action.retry_policy.retry_conditio.rationale: Retry conditions specify which failure types trigger retries (e.g., unavailable, deadline-exceeded). This is resilience and availability configuration, not a security boundary constraint.

rules.matches.description: Matches define conditions used for matching the rule against incoming gRPC requests.

rules.matches.headers.description: Specifies a list of HTTP request headers to match against.

rules.matches.headers.key.description: Required. The key of the header.
rules.matches.headers.key.rationale: Header keys are part of the request matching logic that determines which traffic this rule applies to. They do not constrain what backends can be routed to or the security boundary of the resource.

rules.matches.headers.type.description: The type of match. Default value: "EXACT" Possible values: ["TYPE_UNSPECIFIED", "EXACT", "REGULAR_EXPRESSION"]
rules.matches.headers.type.rationale: Header matching modes (EXACT, REGEX) are functional/architectural configuration without a clear insecure sentinel. ReDoS concerns are speculative and operational, not security properties of this resource.

rules.matches.headers.value.description: Required. The value of the header.
rules.matches.headers.value.rationale: Header values are part of the request matching logic. They determine which traffic is routed by this rule but do not affect the security boundary of the resource itself.

rules.matches.method.description: A gRPC method to match against. If this field is empty or omitted, will match all methods.

rules.matches.method.case_sensitive.description: Specifies that matches are case sensitive. The default value is true.
rules.matches.method.case_sensitive.rationale: Case sensitivity flags are functional/architectural routing configuration. Backend authorization policies enforce actual access control, not this routing flag.

rules.matches.method.grpc_method.description: Required. Name of the method to match against.
rules.matches.method.grpc_method.rationale: gRPC method name determines which operations this rule applies to. This is routing logic, not a security property of this resource—authorization of specific methods is enforced by the backend, not by this route.

rules.matches.method.grpc_service.description: Required. Name of the service to match against.
rules.matches.method.grpc_service.rationale: Service name determines which gRPC service this rule applies to. This is routing configuration, not a security constraint on this resource.
